rules.title: Format rules
rules.intro: The simulator follows the order described by the game wiki and by Liquipedia. Each rule links to its source; what the sources leave out is flagged.
rules.rankedAccess: Draft Pick opens from the Epic rank.
rules.rankedBans: The number of bans depends on the highest rank in the match: {epic} per team in Epic, {legend} in Legend, {mythic} in Mythic and above.
rules.rankedSimultaneous: Both teams ban at the same time, over two rounds, so they can ban the same hero. The sources do not say how many bans fall in each round: the simulator groups them into one.
rules.picks: Picks: blue 1, red 2, blue 2, red 2, blue 2, red 1. A banned or already picked hero cannot be picked.
rules.timers: {ban} seconds to ban, {pick} to pick, per player. When time runs out, the ban stays empty and the pick is random: the game favours the player's most played heroes, which the simulator does not know, so it draws among heroes that fill an open lane.
rules.rankedExample: Order in Mythic; in Epic and Legend only the number of bans changes.
rules.tournamentOrder: Bans are taken in turns, blue team (left) first, then picks in the same order as ranked.
rules.tournamentLimit: On stage, leagues split these bans into two phases with picks in between. Our sources do not publish that order: the simulator sticks to what they document.
rules.bot: The bot bans from the top of the ranking at the chosen rank, which combines win rate and ban rate. For its picks it only keeps heroes that add a lane to its team, ranked on our data at that rank: counters to your picks, duos with its own, win rate. Every choice is explained in one line.
rules.advantage: The summary adds up the win-rate gaps measured in ranked games between the heroes of both teams, plus each team's duo gains. It is an estimate built from those measurements only, not a win probability.

winRate.chapeau: How many wins in a row to reach the win rate you want? Enter your matches and current win rate: everything is computed in your browser, nothing is sent.
winRate.metaDescription: Work out how many consecutive wins you need to reach a target win rate in Mobile Legends: Bang Bang, or how many matches at a given pace.
winRate.methode1: With n matches and w wins, reaching a win rate t takes x straight wins such that (w + x) ÷ (n + x) ≥ t, i.e. x = (t × n − w) ÷ (1 − t), rounded up. The number of wins comes from the win rate shown in game, rounded to two decimals: a match is either won or lost, so it is a whole number.
winRate.methode2: At a pace r above the target, it takes about (t × n − w) ÷ (r − t) matches. If the target is already reached, the calculator shows your margin: how many losses in a row you can take and stay above it.

contribute.chapeau: Game data updates itself; commentary has to be written. Here is how to write a hero analysis and submit it to the site.
contribute.metaDescription: MLBBDex contribution guide: the fields of a hero analysis, an annotated template, style rules and review through a GitHub pull request.
contribute.resume: Write a hero analysis and submit it
contribute.principe1: Roles, lanes, skills, skins, statistics and popular builds come from the automatic sync with the wiki and the community API. An analysis adds only what no extraction produces: what the hero really does, strengths and weaknesses, counters and explained builds.
contribute.principe2: Analyses are written in French, the site's original language. Each one is a TypeScript entry added to the hero's role file in `src/data/heros/`.
contribute.champsIntro: An analysis follows the `AnalyseHeros` type in `src/lib/types.ts`. Its skills and builds each have their own shape.

contribute.modeleIntro: Copy this template to the end of the role file's list, fill it in, then remove its comments. `npm run typecheck` checks it on every run, so it always follows the current type.

style.accents: French accents wherever the language needs them: the analysis text is shown to visitors, even though the project's code goes without.
style.termes: Game terms stay in English: items, skills, talents and spells keep the name players see in game ("Winter Crown", "Flicker").
style.original: Nothing copied: no wiki, guide or video. An analysis taken from elsewhere, even closely reworded, will be rejected.
style.valeurs: No damage values: they change almost every patch. Describe the effect, not the number.
style.concret: Concrete over superlatives: "he wins long fights as long as the enemy doesn't buy healing reduction" beats "he is very strong".

relecture.fork: Fork the GitHub repository and create a branch for your analysis.
relecture.ajout: Add the entry to the role file: `tanks.ts`, `fighters.ts`, `assassins.ts`, `mages.ts`, `marksmen.ts` or `supports.ts`.
relecture.verifier: Run `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm test`. Automated checks will run them again anyway.
relecture.ouvrir: Open a pull request with a clear title in the imperative, in French: "ajoute l'analyse de Ling".
relecture.relire: A maintainer reviews substance and form — accuracy for the current patch, style, originality — and comments on the pull request if something needs to change.
relecture.fusion: Once merged, the analysis goes live with the next deployment, and your name stays in the repository history.

heureServeur.chapeau: Live Mobile Legends server time, and how long is left before each reset: daily at 00:00 server time ({utc} UTC), weekly on Monday, Starlight on the 1st of the month.
heureServeur.fuseauTexte: UTC−8 all year round: server time never switches to daylight saving time.
heureServeur.quotidienneTexte: Every day at 00:00 server time, which is {utc} UTC: daily tasks, new offers and new events.
heureServeur.hebdoTexte: Every Monday at 00:00 server time, which is {utc} UTC on Monday: weekly tasks start over.
heureServeur.starlightTexte: On the 1st of every month at 00:00 server time ({utc} UTC): a new Starlight begins, with its rewards, tasks and shop reset.
heureServeur.saisonTexte: The game dates it in its patch notes, in server time (“S31 will end at 23:59:59 on 3/15”). The countdown picks it up as soon as it is published there.
heureServeur.majTexte: They usually come out between 18:00 and 22:00 server time, which is between {debut} and {fin} UTC the next day.
heureServeur.faq1q: What time is the MLBB daily reset?
heureServeur.faq1r: At {utc} UTC, which is 00:00 server time. In the UK, that is {ete} in summer and {hiver} in winter; in the Philippines, {manille}.
heureServeur.faq2q: Does the server switch to daylight saving time?
heureServeur.faq2r: No: it stays at UTC−8 all year round. If your country observes daylight saving time, your local reset time moves by one hour; the table above accounts for it.
heureServeur.faq3q: When does the ranked season end?
heureServeur.faq3r: The game announces it in its patch notes, in server time. As soon as a date is published there, the countdown above shows it; without an announcement, we don't show an estimated date.

chatiment.chapeau: Train the jungler's reflex: the health bar of the Turtle, the Lord or a buff melts under your team's hits, and you strike as soon as it drops below your Retribution damage, before the enemy jungler does.
chatiment.regle1: Pick an objective, a difficulty and your hero level. The health bar melts under your team's hits; strike (big button, Space or Enter) as soon as HP drops below your Retribution damage.
chatiment.regle2: Too early, Retribution doesn't kill and takes {recharge} s to recharge: the objective is lost. Too slow, the enemy jungler strikes first, or the monster dies without you.
chatiment.regle3: A successful strike is worth up to 1,000 points: {precision} for precision (the share of below-threshold HP still there when you strike) and {vitesse} for speed, full under {pleine} ms and zero beyond {nulle} ms.
chatiment.regle4: A run has {n} rounds. Your best total per objective and difficulty, and your longest streak of successes, stay in your browser. Once the page has been opened, the trainer also works offline.
chatiment.degatsIntro: Retribution deals {base} true damage, plus {parNiveau} per hero level, to creeps and minions. By level:
chatiment.monstresNote: HP at spawn (Turtle, first Lord) or after 12 minutes (Lord, buffs), from the Fandom wiki pages. Buffs are mostly contested mid-game, hence the 12-minute value. Each bar segment is worth 2,000 HP for the Turtle and the Lord, 1,000 for other creeps.
chatiment.valeursEntrainement: Hit rhythm, team damage, bursts and enemy jungler reaction are training values, tuned to feel like a real fight: the game doesn't publish these numbers. Retribution damage and monster HP, however, come from the wiki.
chatiment.sourceChatiment: Fandom wiki, “Retribution” spell: damage by level and cooldown
chatiment.sourceMonstres: Fandom wiki, “Turtle”, “Lord”, “Thunder Fenrir” and “Molten Fiend” pages: initial and 12-minute HP, health bar segments

rangs.chapeau: Every Mobile Legends ranked tier, from Warrior to Mythical Immortal: divisions, stars, Mythic points, draft pick and end-of-season rewards, then the heroes that win most at each rank according to our measurements.
rangs.echelleIntro: {n} tiers, from lowest to highest. A ranked win earns a star and a loss takes one away; past the maximum number of stars you move up a division, and below zero you drop back.
rangs.echelleNote: Draft pick opens at Epic V; below that, ranked games use blind pick. Legend has no emblem in our visuals: a shield stands in for it.
rangs.tableauIntro: The rules of each rank: divisions, stars to earn, draft bans, star-raising and star protection points.
rangs.tableauNote: Star-raising points build up as you play: at 100%, your next win earns an extra star. Star protection points save you a star on a loss. The Mythic family only has protection points.
rangs.mythiqueIntro: Past Legend there are no more divisions: stars become points, and your total sets your tier. {honneur} points take you to Mythical Honor, {gloire} to Mythical Glory, {immortel} to Mythical Immortal.
rangs.mythiquePieces: Reaching 15 points in Mythic earns Mythic Coins each season, the currency of Mythic skins.
rangs.herosTitre: The heroes that win most, rank by rank
rangs.herosIntro: The {n} best win rates in each rank bracket measured by the game, leaving out heroes played too little for their rate to be reliable.
rangs.herosEcart: At the top the ranking shifts: in {rang}, the top list makes room for {noms}, who are outside the all-ranks top list.
rangs.herosNote: These rates come from the tier list and follow each measurement. The game doesn't publish separate figures below Epic.
rangs.remise1: When a season ends, every player starts the new one at a rank set from the one they had reached, and receives that rank's rewards.
rangs.remise2: The reset only applies when you first log in during the new season; your old rank no longer shows on the leaderboard.
rangs.parcours: The Season Journey, open from Epic upwards, rewards the number of ranked games played: the season skin unlocks after 20 games.

quiz.regle2: You get {heros} attempts to find a hero and {objets} for an item. Each miss unlocks a hint and compares your guess with the answer: role, lane, release year, region or price.
quiz.regle3: Your streak, best streak and score distribution stay in your browser. Once you have visited the page, the quiz also works offline.
quiz.regle4: At the end, share your grid: colored squares that give no answer away. Practice mode serves questions without limit.

nickname.title: MLBB Stylish Name Generator
nickname.lead: Type your name and copy it in {n} Unicode styles — bold, gothic, circled, small caps — with decorations like ꧁ ꧂ or 亗. Nothing to install: everything happens in your browser.
nickname.how1: These aren't really fonts: each style swaps Latin letters for other Unicode characters that look like them (mathematical symbols, circled letters, full-width characters). Your nickname stays plain text, so it can be copied, pasted and displayed anywhere the device font knows those characters.
nickname.how2: Only the letters A to Z and digits change. Accents, spaces and symbols stay as they are, and invisible characters (zero-width spaces, direction marks, blank fillers) are removed: the copied nickname contains nothing you can't see.
nickname.rulesTitle: What we know about the game's rules
nickname.rule1: Changing your nickname in Mobile Legends requires a Rename Card, sold in the in-game shop.
nickname.rule2: Neither Moonton nor the MLBB wiki publishes the allowed length or the list of accepted characters. A third-party guide reports {min} to {max} characters: the counter uses that as a guide and blocks nothing.
nickname.rule3: We also don't know how the game counts. A “𝐀” is one Unicode character but two UTF-16 units, and the strikethrough style adds one character per letter: the counter shows both measures, and a stylish nickname may hit the limit sooner than a plain one.
nickname.rule4: A symbol missing from the game's font shows up as an empty box. Without an official list, we can't guarantee a style will be accepted: try a few.
nickname.q1: Why does my nickname show up as boxes?
nickname.a1: The device or game font doesn't include those characters. The rarer the character, the more likely it's missing: try another style or decoration.
nickname.a2: No. The conversion happens in your browser; nothing is sent or stored.
nickname.q3: Can I use these nicknames outside MLBB?
nickname.a3: Yes: they're standard Unicode characters that most apps can display. Screen readers often read them poorly, though: keep that in mind if your teammates use one.

drawCalculator.title: MLBB Draw Calculator
drawCalculator.lead: How many diamonds for an event skin? Enter the price per draw, the prize chance and the pity: your odds for your budget, the average, and the 50, 90 and 99% milestones.
drawCalculator.method1: Each draw is treated as independent, with the same chance p of getting the prize. The chance of having it within n draws is 1 − (1 − p)ⁿ; with a guarantee on draw N, it reaches 100% on the Nth draw.
drawCalculator.method2: The average number of draws is (1 − (1 − p)ᴺ) / p with a guarantee, 1 / p without. The price uses the cheapest mix of 10-draws and single draws; the average in diamonds is given for both ways of drawing.
drawCalculator.method3: One-off discounts (half-price first draw of the day, discount weeks), free tokens and weekly milestone rewards aren't counted: they lower the real cost.
drawCalculator.method4: A Crystal of Aurora replaces one diamond in draws: count them together in your budget.
drawCalculator.limit1: The game often gives the chance for a category (“a skin”, 1%) rather than for a specific skin. If the skin you want is one of several, its chance is lower: enter it if the event publishes it.
drawCalculator.limit2: Some events aren't simple draws: a price that rises with each draw (Grand Collection), points to build up (Zodiac), cores to exchange (Magic Wheel). This calculation doesn't apply to them.
drawCalculator.findTitle: Where to find an event's odds
drawCalculator.find1: Moonton displays the probabilities of every draw in game, with the event's rules. The MLBB wiki copies some of them: the calculator's presets come from there, with the page date, because rules can change.
drawCalculator.q1: Do {draws} draws at {p} guarantee the prize?
drawCalculator.a1: No. Each draw starts from scratch: {draws} draws at {p} give a {chance} chance, and it takes {n} to reach 99%, unless a guarantee kicks in sooner.
drawCalculator.q2: Is it better to draw 10 at a time?
drawCalculator.a2: When the 10-draw costs less than ten single draws, the price per draw goes down; but if the prize drops early, you've still paid for the rest of the 10-draw. The calculator gives the average for both.
drawCalculator.q3: Does the pity reset after a prize?
drawCalculator.a3: It depends on the event: read its rules. The calculation covers the first prize you get, where the question doesn't arise.

roam.step2: Head to the Turtle before {turtle}: the roamer comes to help take it.

exp.step2: For the first {waves} waves, your lane's cannon minion gives {expBonus}% extra EXP.

buildSimulator.title: Build simulator
buildSimulator.lead: Put a build together — hero, level, six items, emblem, talents and spell — and read its computed stats, source by source. The page link keeps the build: copy it to share.
buildSimulator.method1: Hero base stats come from the wiki, which only publishes them at levels 1 and 15: in between they are interpolated in a straight line, which remains an approximation. HP regen is only given at level 1, and base attack speed is not listed at all: only the percentage bonus is shown.
buildSimulator.method2: Item attributes are read from their wiki pages, emblem and talent figures from its “Emblems” page. A unique attribute only counts once per item, a passive with the same name on two items only works once, and two pairs of boots do not stack: the simulator flags it. Conditional passives (below an HP threshold, after a skill…) are listed but not counted.
buildSimulator.method3: Caps applied: 40% cooldown reduction, 45% with Enchanted Talisman's Magic Mastery passive, and 100% crit chance. Crit damage starts at 200%. The game caps attack speed at 3 attacks per second, which cannot be applied without a base speed.
buildSimulator.method4: Effective HP divides HP by the game's damage multiplier, 120 / (120 + defense). The damage reference applies the same formula to a target's defense after penetration: defense × (1 − % penetration) − flat penetration, never below −60.
buildSimulator.method5: Measured builds come from the game's academy, relayed by arena.rone.dev: for each hero, lane and rank, the three core items of the most played builds, with their win rate and share of games. The simulator shows those sharing at least two items with yours.

blocs.p: The full roster, every hero's skins, items, emblems, Battle Spells and the list of patches. This data is extracted automatically from the community wiki every week: a new hero shows up here without anyone having to enter it.

On top of that comes what no extraction will ever produce: a written analysis for some of the heroes — what they actually do, their builds, their counters — a tier list where every placement is justified, and in-depth guides.

blocs.h: What it doesn't contain, and why

blocs.p: No player rankings and no “MMR”. Moonton publishes no official interface: the stats shown here — win, ban and pick rates, counters, builds, trends — come from the community API arena.rone.dev, which aggregates ranked games by rank. Sites that show an “MMR” for Mobile Legends estimate it; they don't read it from anywhere.

Once logged in with the in-game verification code, you see your own profile — season, heroes played, recent matches — read on demand through that same API, for you only. It is neither published nor kept beyond a cache of a few minutes.

The visuals belong to Moonton. Portraits, icons and skin artwork come from the community wiki and are served by this site so that nothing depends on a third-party domain. They remain Moonton's property, are included for illustration purposes, and will be removed at the rights holder's request. The site's visual identity — midnight blue, gold, cut corners — is inspired by the game's without reusing its interface files.

The roundup section automatically gathers posts about the game from other sites. It only shows the title, the date and a short excerpt, and always links back to the original publisher: nothing is republished here.

Moonton publishes no official feed — the game's website is an app whose content can't be syndicated. Game updates are therefore reproduced and commented by hand in the patch notes, while the roundup covers what the rest of the web publishes.

It's optional: all content is accessible without logging in. Logging in uses Moonton's official verification code — a four-digit code sent to your in-game mailbox. The site never sees your password: it receives a temporary token, stored in a secure cookie, which you delete when you log out.

No account is created on the site. Your favorite heroes stay in your browser. Only notifications, if you turn them on, keep your browser's push address and your list of favorites on the server: the privacy page details what is stored and how to delete it.
The code and content are public. Hero profiles live in typed TypeScript files, articles in Markdown files: you can add a profile or fix a mistake without knowing the rest of the project.
[The repository is here.]({depot}) Balance fixes, missing profiles and proofreading are especially welcome.

Data processing and the use of cookies are detailed in the [privacy policy](/privacy).
This site is designed to work without storing personal data on a server: it has no account database. This page describes the little that is processed, and where.
Only one cookie can be set, and only if you connect your game account:

ul: `mlbb_jeu` — session cookie strictly necessary for login. It contains the temporary token issued by the Moonton service, never leaves the server (`httpOnly`), and expires on its own. If you don't log in, no cookie is set.

blocs.p: As this cookie is strictly necessary for the service you request (staying logged in), it doesn't require prior consent. No advertising or tracking cookies are used.
Your favorite heroes are saved in your browser's local storage (`localStorage`), on your device only. They are not sent to any server and never leave this browser. Clearing the site data erases them.

Login uses Moonton's official flow: you provide your game ID and server, a verification code is sent to you in-game, and the site receives a temporary token in return. These exchanges go through a community API (`arena.rone.dev`) and Moonton's authentication service. The site stores none of this information: the token lives in the session cookie, on the browser side, and disappears when you log out or when it expires. You are never asked for a password.

The images (portraits, icons, emblems) are served by Moonton's and the community wiki's hosts. Loading a page therefore sends requests to these services, which can see your IP address, as with any remote resource.
If audience measurement is enabled, it uses a cookie-free tool that collects no personal data and doesn't track visitors from one site to another. No consent banner is needed in that case.

Since the site keeps no personal data file, there is nothing to access, correct or delete on the server side. You stay in control of what lives in your browser (favorites, session) by logging out or clearing the site data. For any question, write to [{contact}](mailto:{contact}).

push.usage: This data is used only to let you know when a patch changes one of these heroes. It is not linked to any account or name and is shared with no one; notification content is encrypted all the way to your browser, and only your browser's push service delivers it.
push.desabonner: To unsubscribe, turn off the switch in your favorites, or the bell next to the favorite button on a hero page: this data is then deleted from the server. Blocking the site's notifications in your browser or clearing its data also stops them; the subscription, now invalid, is deleted at the next notification.

impure-rage.description: The next skill deals extra damage and restores mana.

quantum-charge.description: Skill damage grants movement speed and healing.
quantum-charge.pourQui: Heroes who need to stay mobile in fights.

weapon-master.description: Increases all attack bonuses gained from items.
weapon-master.pourQui: Fighters whose damage comes from skills.

lethal-ignition.description: Deals extra damage to a badly wounded target.
lethal-ignition.pourQui: Carries who need to finish fights fast.

concussive-blast.description: Deals area damage based on max HP.

wilderness-blessing.description: Increases movement speed out of combat and in bushes.
wilderness-blessing.pourQui: Roamers who live in the bushes, like Franco.

focusing-mark.description: Targets hit take more damage from allies.
focusing-mark.pourQui: Supports and tanks who play for their carry.

brave-smite.description: Hitting an enemy with a skill restores HP.

killing-spree.description: A takedown restores HP and grants movement speed.

bargain-hunter.pourQui: Roamers, whose income is the lowest on the team.

pull-yourself-together.description: Reduces the cooldown of Battle Spells and active items.

flicker.description: Teleports the hero a short distance.
flicker.pourQui: Almost everyone: initiating, escaping, animation canceling.

execute.description: Deals damage based on the target's missing HP.
execute.pourQui: Junglers and assassins who need to secure kills.

retribution.description: Deals heavy damage to a monster and speeds up jungle clearing.

purify.description: Removes crowd control effects and grants brief immunity.
purify.pourQui: Carries targeted by a single crowd control: against Chou, Franco, Kaja.

inspire.description: Greatly increases attack speed and ignores part of the target's armor.
inspire.pourQui: Marksmen that rely on basic attacks.

sprint.description: Increases movement speed and removes slows.
sprint.pourQui: Heroes without mobility who need to reposition.

arrival.description: Teleports the hero to an allied turret or minion.
arrival.pourQui: Solo laners who need to get back quickly after recalling.

vengeance.description: Reflects part of the damage taken for the duration.

aegis.description: Grants a shield to yourself and nearby allies.

revitalize.description: Creates an area that heals allies inside it.
revitalize.pourQui: Supports facing damage spread over time.

outilTaux.invalide: Enter a whole number of matches (at least one) and win rates between 0 and 100%.
outilTaux.phraseVictoires: Without a single loss, {n} wins in a row take your win rate from {actuel} to {objectif}, for {total} matches in total.
outilTaux.impossible: A 100% win rate means never having lost: after one loss, no winning streak can bring you all the way back.
outilTaux.impossibleConseil: For {objectif}, {n} wins in a row are enough.
outilTaux.phraseAtteint: Target already reached: you can lose {n} matches in a row and stay at {objectif} or above.
outilTaux.phraseLimite: Target reached with no margin: your next loss will take you below {objectif}.
outilTaux.phraseZero: No losing streak can take a win rate below 0%.
outilTaux.base: Based on {v} wins out of {n} matches. The game rounds the win rate it shows; the number of wins is a whole number.
outilTaux.rythmeIntro: Over time, your win rate moves towards the one you keep up match after match. Enter one to see how many matches it will take.
outilTaux.rythmeParties: About {n} matches at a {rythme} win rate to reach the target.
outilTaux.rythmeInsuffisant: At a {rythme} win rate, you will never get above {objectif}: you need to win more often than the target.

aideDifficulte.facile: Slow, steady hits, threshold marker and HP shown. The enemy jungler takes over a second to react.
aideDifficulte.normal: Real fight pace, a few enemy bursts. Marker and HP still shown.
aideDifficulte.difficile: Fast, uneven hits, frequent bursts. No marker, no HP numbers: read the bar.
aideDifficulte.pro: The enemy jungler strikes within 300–420 ms: you have to anticipate the hit that crosses the threshold.
